requirements.text: Start at https://books.toscrape.com/ and follow every category link of the side list except the top-level "Books" one.
On each category page, follow its book links and its "next" page link, the next page keeping the same category name.
On each book page record one item with the title, the price as a decimal number of pounds, the stock as an integer, the rating 1-5 and the page's address.
The item's category name is passed along from the category page (request data), not read again on the book page.
Stay on the site (off-site links are not followed).
Store the items in a named dataset and export it to a JSON file when the crawl ends.
Report how many pages succeeded, failed and were skipped, with honest counts.
Report, for each failed or skipped page, why it failed or was skipped.
A book page missing a field is not recorded with an invented value: it ends failed or skipped with its reason (failure point 3).

programs.notes: The final program is only the placeholder comment '// Your TypeScript program goes here'; the task was not attempted.

api_misuses.assumed: the crawl declaration lives in the Collie client
api_misuses.doc_says: AsyncCrawl and AsyncCrawlContext are declared in goodfetch_foxhound; the Collie client exports neither
crawl.label returns a Label[P]; handlers are registered with @crawl.handle(label). Labels are also declared twice with the same name

api_misuses.assumed: a class method starting a crawl from dict seeds
api_misuses.doc_says: no such member; a Run is started with foxhound.start_crawl(crawl, seeds=[seed(url, label)]) on a connected AsyncFoxhound

api_misuses.assumed: members waiting for the end and holding lists and a failures dict
api_misuses.doc_says: invented; the Run ends with finish() returning CrawlRunReport (report.requests counts) and outcomes(kinds=...) gives each failed/skipped reason

api_misuses.assumed: the handler must load its own request
api_misuses.doc_says: the handler's page already holds the request's response

api_misuses.assumed: clicking the next link queues the next category page
api_misuses.doc_says: a click navigates the handler's page and enqueues nothing; following needs ctx.enqueue / enqueue_links with a Label

api_misuses.assumed: a plain dict payload for a Label typed BookItem
api_misuses.doc_says: payload must be the Label's payload type (BookItem); a partial dict fails the payload schema

api_misuses.assumed: every error, including a missing field, becomes a skip
api_misuses.doc_says: skip ends the request skipped, but the catch-all also swallows real failures (HTTP errors, timeouts) into skips, so failed counts are not honest

site_errors: book links found by role link with name matching 'book'
price/stock via get_by_text labels of the product table
rating by counting 'star' in the class instead of mapping its word
home page seeded as a category page, no side-list category selection
programs.notes: Uses invented or misplaced members throughout (no handle, no start_crawl, no finish, no export) and never follows the home page's category links, so no crawl would run; it writes its own counts file instead of exporting a named Dataset.
No final program exists at the named path (the run folder holds no s05_two_page_crawl.rs); the task was not delivered.
